title: RD black screen: h264_nvenc_cuda scale_cuda fails at runtime (CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND) on RTX 5080
description: h264_nvenc_cuda codec uses -vf hwupload_cuda,scale_cuda=format=nv12. scale_cuda CANNOT convert RGB(BGRA)->NV12 in any prebuilt Windows ffmpeg (Gyan AND BtbN both ship --enable-cuda-llvm, whose Clang-compiled scale_cuda lacks the RGB->semiplanar kernel). FFmpeg passes init then dies at RUNTIME: 'cuModuleGetFunction ... CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND: named symbol not found' / 'Unsupported conversion: rgb0 -> semiplanar8' -> pipe ends -> 0fps black screen. The init-based codec fallback never triggers (failure is at runtime). Reproduced directly via ffmpeg testsrc on the 5080. FIX: NVENC ingests bgra/bgr0 NATIVELY (confirmed in supported pixfmts + test) and does RGB->YUV in fixed-function HW, so feed BGRA straight to h264_nvenc (no scale_cuda, no CPU swscale). Rename codec h264_nvenc_cuda -> h264_nvenc_bgra. Verified working via direct ffmpeg test.
close_reason: Fixed: GPU codec path rewritten from broken hwupload_cuda,scale_cuda=format=nv12 (scale_cuda lacks RGB->NV12 kernel in all cuda-llvm Windows ffmpeg builds -> runtime CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND -> FFmpeg death -> black screen) to direct BGRA->h264_nvenc (NVENC native HW color convert). Verified via exact agent encode args at 2560x1440 and 4096x1152. Deployed.

title: RD: frame-derived dimension contract (fix first-connect zoom + pixel-perfect mouse)
description:
Root cause: host sends size metadata (SendCurrentStreamBootstrapAsync, RemoteDesktopHandler.cs:215) BEFORE the capture loop starts (StreamFramesAsync, :232). DxgiDesktopCapture defers DuplicateOutput to the first frame, so GetScreenSize() races init and GetActiveBounds() falls through to GetVirtualDesktopBounds() (both monitors). Android letterboxes + maps mouse to wrong dims; user must switch monitors to force a re-bootstrap. WarmUpCapture (RemEx-6my) tried to win the race and did not.

Fix (robust, backend-agnostic): derive the dimension contract from the FIRST ACTUAL captured frame (encoded pixel w/h + source monitor absolute virtual-desktop rect), send metadata AFTER that frame, re-send on any change; single-source so mouse-map + video letterbox use identical numbers; resolve target to PRIMARY monitor before first frame (never silently stream virtual desktop); make process PerMonitorV2 DPI-aware (app.manifest has none) so capture+monitor rects+SendInput agree in physical px. Android: re-fit on authoritative dim change instead of locking on stale dims; landscape=primary fully visible, portrait=fit-to-height. Supersedes the timing patches in RemEx-6my/2i5/gd7.
close_reason: Verified on-device: first connect renders the full 2560x1440 primary monitor at 120fps NVENC with no multi-monitor workaround. Host bootstrap logs correct dims (2560x1440 @ 0,0).

IMAGE FIX (headline) in remex.android H264StreamDecoder.kt: (1) in steady-state loop inspect each AU for SPS (reuse findNalUnits/NAL_TYPE_SPS), compare SPS NAL bytes to configured csd-0; on change codec.stop/configure(newFormat,surface,null,0)/start with new csd-0/csd-1. Fixes scale-up black/garbage. title: RemEx.Host desktop capture (Desktop Duplication/DWM-redirect) crashes NVIDIA driver — black screen + cursor, host machine soft-locked
description:
LIVE INCIDENT 2026-06-22: leftover RemEx.Host dev processes (PIDs 5188 + 17816; one had burned 286 CPU-s) were actively screen-capturing and crashed the NVIDIA display driver + DWM, leaving the host at a black screen with only the mouse cursor. Ctrl+Alt+Del and Win+Ctrl+Shift+B could not recover (display stack wedged below the input layer).

EVIDENCE (Windows logs):
- App Event 1000: dwm.exe crashed in dwmredir.dll (DWM screen-redirection / capture path) @ 03:53:50
- WER LKD bucket 'LKD_0x1B8_NV_Blackscreen_Blackbox_dxgkrnl!DxgCreateLiveDumpWithDriverBlob' @ 05:11:02 (NVIDIA black-screen live kernel dump)
- WER LKD bucket 'LKD_0x1A8_KEYBD_HOTKEY_OSGraphicsMonitorPower' @ 05:11:17 (user's Win+Ctrl+Shift+B GPU-reset hotkey captured as a dump; GPU too hung to recover)

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION APPLIED: stopped RemexHost service, set StartType=Manual, killed RemEx.Host processes, restarted DWM to recover the compositor. Service is OFF/Manual until fixed.

ROOT-CAUSE TO INVESTIGATE (capture path in Remex.Host): Desktop Duplication device-lost / DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED / ACCESS_LOST handling, DWM-redirect usage, and the runaway-CPU capture loop (286 CPU-s on one PID suggests a hot spin). Capturing the desktop must NEVER be able to take down the host GPU/driver. Needs device-lost recovery, backpressure/frame pacing, and a watchdog that tears down capture instead of spinning.

REPRO HINT: NVIDIA GPU + RemEx.Host running desktop capture for an extended idle period.
close_reason: Root cause: DxgiDesktopCapture re-created the DXGI duplication (DuplicateOutput) on every DXGI_ERROR_ACCESS_LOST, throttling only on re-init exceptions. Since access-loss returns the cached frame, the stream loop saw 'success' and never backed off, so DuplicateOutput ran at full frame rate (up to 120Hz) against a display mid power-transition (idle monitor-off), wedging DWM (dwmredir.dll) + the NVIDIA driver -> host black-screen-with-cursor, CAD/Win+Ctrl+Shift+B unrecoverable. Fix: new DuplicationReinitThrottle rate-limits re-init (1 attempt per escalating 1s->8s window, reset by any healthy frame) wired into TryReinitializeDuplication + TryRecover; healthy-frame reset added to both capture paths + cursor-shape refresh. 8 unit tests pass; no regressions (the 11 other failures are pre-existing, tracked separately). CHANGELOG updated. Defense-in-depth display-power gating filed as follow-up.

title: Concurrent NSD resolve race (FAILURE_ALREADY_ACTIVE) + leaked resolve coroutine

title: Unbounded encoder output queue + accumulator buffer -> OOM / latency blowup
description: Boundary: RemoteDesktop. FFmpegH264Encoder.cs: (1) ReaderLoop acc Array.Resize-doubled w/ no cap (262-265) — malformed Annex-B w/o AUD never cuts -> unbounded growth. (2) _encodedFrames unbounded ConcurrentQueue (line 19) enqueues all (283), EncodeFrame dequeues only 1/call (335); StreamFramesAsync never drains via TryGetEncodedFrame -> pile-up, memory+latency growth. Fix: cap acc (reset stream past few MB w/o AUD); bounded Channel<byte[]> drop-oldest, or drain fully each capture iteration keeping newest.

title: Dropped decoder input frames cause persistent corruption; no keyframe recovery
description: Boundary: RemoteDesktop. H264StreamDecoder.kt:75-92 dequeueInputBuffer(10000); on index<0 the access-unit is silently dropped (no else/retry/queue). H.264 P-frame drop desyncs until next IDR; GOP fixed 60 (FFmpegH264Encoder.cs:150 -g 60) and forceKeyframe is a no-op (EncodeFrame 310-314) so no on-demand recovery -> up to ~1s green/frozen corruption, indefinite if IDR missed. Fix: bounded retry before drop; MediaCodec async setCallback w/ bounded input queue; host keyframe-request message + real force_key_frames.

title: Blocking ffmpeg stdin write hangs capture thread past cancellation on disconnect
description: Boundary: RemoteDesktop. FFmpegH264Encoder.EncodeFrame (FFmpegH264Encoder.cs:323) does blocking _stdin.Write+Flush, no timeout/token; called from capture task (RemoteDesktopHandler.cs:376). If HW encoder stalls / downstream slow, OS pipe (~64KB) fills, Write blocks; on disconnect ct cancelled but thread parked in native Write, never checks it. Fix: write on dedicated thread via Stream.WriteAsync(buffer,ct) with timeout, or bounded Channel<byte[]> between capture and stdin writer with drop-on-full.

title: Throwing catch block in Export escapes JNI boundary -> NativeAOT abort
description: Boundary: JNI. AndroidNativeExports.cs Export catch (1138) calls CreateJString(SerializeOperationFailure(...)); SerializeOperationFailure (1164) runs JsonSerializer.Serialize which can throw (OOM); exception thrown FROM the catch escapes the UnmanagedCallersOnly export -> runtime abort. Fix: wrap catch body in its own try{return CreateJString(...);}catch{return IntPtr.Zero;} symmetric with the void-path hardening.

title: Oversize /ws message throws uncaught InvalidOperationException, bypassing connection cleanup
description: Boundary: RemexMessage /ws. MessageSerializer.cs:72-73 throws InvalidOperationException over 4MB. PingPongHandler.cs receive loop catches only OperationCanceledException/WebSocketException (301-308); HostBootstrapper.cs:386 not wrapped. Exception escapes -> cleanup block (310-331: file-transfer cleanup, pairing cancel, telemetry stream-cts) bypassed -> orphaned telemetry task + leaked transfer state per hostile message. Fix: ReceiveAsync drain-and-return-null instead of throw; add catch(InvalidOperationException); wrap cleanup in finally.

title: Pending Java exception not cleared across UnmanagedCallersOnly export -> JVM abort
description: Boundary: JNI. JniHelper.ReadJString (JniHelper.cs:32-59) calls GetStringLength/GetStringChars with no ExceptionCheck; on JVM exception (e.g. OOM) returns null with pending exception. Export (AndroidNativeExports.cs:1130-1141) try only catches MANAGED exceptions; pending Java exception survives the return and the next JNI call (CreateJString/NewString) while pending = JNI spec violation -> SIGABRT. Fix: ExceptionCheck+ExceptionClear at export prologue and in ReadJString before returning null.

title: Unbounded concurrent TCP connections + no handshake/read timeout on 8338 (DoS)
description: Boundary: 8338. RemexNetworkListener.AcceptClientsAsync (line 174-184) does _ = HandleClientSafeAsync in a tight loop, no SemaphoreSlim/Channel cap; TLS handshake (241) and ReadExactlyAsync (271,283) have no timeout. N concurrent conns each alloc up to MaxPayloadSize(10MB) -> N*10MB unbounded; slow-loris holds tasks. Fix: SemaphoreSlim(maxConcurrent) gate; linked CTS timeout around handshake+reads; reject at capacity.

title: Single-threaded IPC accept loop — one hung client wedges the auth/PIN channel (DoS)
description: Boundary: Named Pipe IPC. LocalIpcServerService.cs:114-120 awaits HandleClientAsync inline before re-accept; read at 147 has only shutdown token, no per-op timeout. A client that connects and never writes parks the only PIN/power channel until shutdown. Fix: fire-and-forget HandleClientAsync (_ = ...) + immediate re-accept (as IpcHostServer.cs:79 does); add read timeout via linked CTS CancelAfter.

title: Host TLS private key exported to passwordless, world-readable PFX
description: Boundary: pairing/cert. CertificateService.cs:134-144: File.WriteAllBytes PFX then SetUnixFileMode (Linux only, after = TOCTOU); no Windows ACL, ProgramData grants Users:Read; PFX has no password (Export(Pfx) / LoadPkcs12FromFile null). Any local user reads host key, impersonates host, SPKI pin matches -> MITM all sessions. Fix: write temp w/ 0600 then move (Linux); explicit FileSecurity LocalSystem+Administrators (Windows); or DPAPI/X509Store LocalMachine.

title: No brute-force throttling on 6-digit PIN verification
description: Boundary: pairing. PairingService.VerifyClientHmacCoreAsync (PairingService.cs:155-202) on mismatch (187-189) logs+returns false but does NOT cancel session/count failures/backoff. Session valid for PairingTimeoutSeconds=600. 10^6 PIN space exhaustible within 10-min window via repeated pairing_complete. Fix: failure counter -> CancelPairingCore after N(5); shorten TTL to 60-120s; per-IP throttle on /ws and /start-pairing.

title: RemExLocalIPC pipe grants Everyone ReadWrite; leaks pairing PIN + power commands to any local user

ExecuteCommandAsync (182-256) dispatches SHUTDOWN/RESTART/etc and GETPAIRINGPIN (230-239)/STARTPAIRING (241-249) returning live PairingPinInfo to ANY local caller, no impersonation check. Fix: grant LocalSystem FullControl + Interactive SID ReadWrite only; verify caller via GetImpersonationUserName/RunAsClient before state-changing/secret commands.

title: Unauthenticated /start-pairing and /pairing-pin disclose PIN to remote callers

title: 8338 TCP command port dispatches power commands with NO client authentication
description: Boundary: TCP(TLS) script ingress port 8338. RemexNetworkListener binds IPAddress.Any (Remex.Core/Services/Network/RemexNetworkListener.cs:94), runs as live hosted service (ExternalNetworkListenerService, HostBootstrapper.cs:96). AuthenticateAsServerAsync uses clientCertificateRequired:false (line 243); comment lines 307-308 'Access key validation removed in 2.0 ... pairing verification deferred' then calls ExecuteCommandAsync (line 309) with zero authn. Any LAN/remote host completing TLS can issue SHUTDOWN/FORCESHUTDOWN/RESTART/SLEEP/LOCK/WAKEONLAN. Confirmation: traced source 230-319. Fix: bind loopback OR require PairedClientRegistry token / client-cert pinning before dispatch.

title: DXGI Desktop Duplication opens eagerly at host startup; idle service holds duplication slot
description: Root cause behind the eager-init family (see RemEx-crk for the original throttle fix). DxgiDesktopCapture ctor (DxgiDesktopCapture.cs:243-244) calls InitializeDevice()+InitializeDuplication()->DuplicateOutput immediately. It is forced on every host boot because HostCapabilitiesProvider takes IScreenCaptureService as a ctor dependency and HostBootstrapper resolves IHostCapabilitiesProvider eagerly (HostBootstrapper.cs:238). Result: the auto-start RemexHost service holds a Desktop Duplication consumer slot at idle with no client, contending with Windows' own remote desktop ('something watching'). Fix B: defer DXGI init to first capture via idempotent lock-held EnsureInitialized() in TryCapture/TryCaptureRaw/TryRecover; capabilities/diagnostics become a cheap probe that never opens duplication. Wire-format SupportsRemoteDesktop unchanged (independent of DXGI). Related: RemEx-crk.

title: Remote desktop renders cursor only - frame path silently dies (freshness-bit root cause)
description: Remote desktop shows the cursor but no live screen content. Cursor renders from a separate stream (desktop_cursor_shape/state -> Canvas overlay) so 'cursor but no screen' = frame path silently dying. Verified root-cause candidate: DxgiDesktopCapture returns its cached _lastFrame indistinguishably on DXGI_ERROR_ACCESS_LOST (~12 sites) and RemoteDesktopHandler.cs:383 counts any non-empty buffer as captureSucceeded=true, so a stale replay counts as success and the 5-failure coded-error path never trips. Load-bearing fix: thread a freshness signal capture->handler->consecutiveFailures so stale replays stop counting as success, and emit a coded error on genuine stall. Driven by the Looper loop at looper-output/ (remote-desktop-frame-fix). Excludes (mechanically gated out): pairing/cert/RemexMessage-envelope/Named-Pipe. 8 failure-mode enum + 7-scenario human matrix in loop.yaml.

Threaded an IsLive signal capture->handler via additive IScreenCaptureService.CaptureRawScreenLiveAsync/CaptureScreenLiveAsync + ScreenCaptureResult struct (no protocolVersion bump). DxgiDesktopCapture.TryCapture/TryCaptureRaw now report stale=false on ACCESS_LOST/SESSION_DISCONNECTED/error replays, live=true on fresh frames + healthy-static (WAIT_TIMEOUT/AccumulatedFrames==0, preserving bandwidth reuse). RemoteDesktopHandler skips stale replays so a frozen output advances consecutiveFailures and emits coded desktop_error. New seam test DesktopStart_WhenCaptureReplaysStaleFrames_SendsCodedCaptureError passes; host 283/284 (1 unrelated pre-existing RemEx-syz), core 108/108. title: Android never persists/supplies PAIR-1 reconnect secret -> host rejects all reconnects
description: 2.0 hardening (fe71162, PAIR-1) added proof-of-possession on reconnect: host sends a ReconnectChallenge nonce and requires HMAC-SHA256(reconnectSecret,nonce); a bare clientId no longer authenticates. Host + C# native client (RemexNativeClient.RespondToReconnectChallenge, AndroidNativeInitRequest.ReconnectSecret) were updated and the secret is returned to Kotlin in the pairing result (AndroidNativeExports: 'OK:hostId|spki|reconnectSecret'). BUT the Kotlin layer never persisted it: RemexClientManager pairing block reads only parts[0]/parts[1] and drops parts[2]; the InitRemex JSON omits reconnectSecret. So _reconnectSecretBase64 is null natively, RespondToReconnectChallenge early-returns, no ReconnectProof is sent, and the host rejects every request ('Rejecting process_list_request from unpaired connection'). Pre-2.0 this worked because a bare clientId authenticated (opening Task Manager sent the first command and the host trusted the clientId). Fix: persist the reconnect secret per-host in PinnedHostStore (Tink-encrypted) on pairing, and include it as 'reconnectSecret' in the InitRemex JSON on connect. Clients paired before the fix must re-pair once.

title: Android NSD resolve crashes app (RejectedExecutionException) when executor is shut down with callbacks pending
description: NsdDiscoveryManager.resolveServiceModern (API 34+ path, used by the user's Galaxy S24/Android 14+) creates Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor(), passes it to NsdManager.registerServiceInfoCallback, then cleanup() unregisters and immediately calls executor.shutdown(). unregisterServiceInfoCallback is async; NSD still posts a final callback (e.g. onServiceInfoCallbackUnregistered) to the executor after shutdown. The default AbortPolicy throws RejectedExecutionException inside NsdManager$ServiceHandler.handleMessage on the system ConnectivityThread -> uncatchable FATAL -> whole app crashes ('RemEx has stopped'). Repeating crash (logcat 21:35, 21:36, 22:52-22:57) -> this is the 'session closed' half of the user's connection failure, independent of the host-side PIN fix (RemEx-dqj). Fix: use a single-thread ThreadPoolExecutor with DiscardPolicy so post-shutdown posts are silently dropped instead of throwing. Requires APK rebuild + reinstall to deploy.

title: Pairing persistence throws (SID not allowed to be owner) when Remex.Host runs interactively
description: PairedClientRegistry.RestrictStorePermissionsWindows calls FileSecurity.SetOwner(LocalSystem) on paired_clients.json (PAIR-4 hardening). When the host runs as the signed-in user instead of the LocalSystem service, assigning LocalSystem as owner needs SeRestorePrivilege (absent even for elevated admins), so SetAccessControl throws InvalidOperationException 'The security identifier is not allowed to be the owner of this object'. RestrictStorePermissions only catches IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException/PlatformNotSupportedException, so it escapes PersistToDisk->RegisterClient and breaks pairing persistence in interactive mode (also fails 11 Remex.Host.Tests). Fix: choose an assignable owner (current user when not LocalSystem), grant ACL to user+LocalSystem+Admins, and broaden the best-effort catch so hardening failure never blocks pairing. Same regression family as RemEx-dqj (fe71162).

title: Pairing PIN rejected when Remex.Host runs interactively (WTSQueryUserToken requires LocalSystem)

When the merged Avalonia host runs interactively as the signed-in user (RemexHost service stopped), WTSQueryUserToken fails (proven: err 1314 PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD), the check returns null, and ALL privileged IPC commands (GETPAIRINGPIN, GENERATEPAIRINGPIN, SHUTDOWN, ...) are rejected. The host UI never gets a PIN to display, so Android pairing fails with 'invalid PIN'. Regression introduced by fe71162 (IPC-1 hardening). Fix: secure fallback that treats the host's own identity as the console user when the host process runs in the active console session as a non-system user.

title: protocolVersion enforced with divergent policies on /ws (<2) vs /ws/desktop (!=2)

Host bumps _encoderConfigVersion and rebuilds ffmpeg with new -s WxH (incl ClampScaleForH264 4096 cap, RemoteDesktopHandler.cs:1243) emitting new SPS/PPS; decoder only recreated when streamPixelWidth/Height-keyed AndroidView rebuilds, not on slider-driven encoded-size change. title: Orphaned ffmpeg stderr-reader tasks leak on encoder rebuild churn
description: Boundary: RemoteDesktop. FFmpegH264Encoder.cs:222-234 stderr drain Task.Run loops while(!process.HasExited) ReadLineAsync with no CancellationToken; on encoder rebuilds (quality/scale slider bumps _encoderConfigVersion -> TryCreateH264Encoder, RemoteDesktopHandler.cs:325-342) each spawns a detached task referencing the disposed encoder's _logger; self-terminates on Kill but stacks up under churn. title: mDNS address selection is Windows-centric, single-IPv4; under-advertises on multi-NIC/Linux
description: Boundary: mDNS advertising. MdnsAdvertisingService.cs: TryGetPrimaryIpv4Address (102) returns ONE address (yield break 88); interface filter (128-132) excludes by Windows description substrings (WSL/Hyper-V/vEthernet/Virtual) with no Linux equivalents (docker0/virbr0/tailscale0/wg0); IPv6 filtered out (137). Multi-homed Linux box advertises only default-route IPv4 -> clients on secondary segment can't discover. Cross-platform divergence. Fix: advertise all preferred unicast addresses; add Linux virtual-iface filters; optionally link-local-safe IPv6.

title: Host mDNS advertises once; no re-advertise on network/address change
description: Boundary: mDNS advertising. MdnsAdvertisingService.cs: GetAdvertisableAddresses evaluated once at start (36), advertise once (55), then Task.Delay(Timeout.Infinite) (58). No NetworkChange.NetworkAddressChanged subscription. DHCP renew / Wi-Fi<->Ethernet / VPN change silently breaks discovery while service shows 'running'. Fix: subscribe NetworkChange.NetworkAddressChanged; on change Unadvertise+rebuild addresses+Advertise; honor stoppingToken to unsubscribe.

title: IPC pipe has no message framing/length validation — 8192 truncation / partial-read corruption
description: Boundary: Named Pipe IPC. LocalIpcServerService.cs:146-150 single ReadAsync into byte[8192] treated as whole request (Byte transmission mode, no length prefix, no read loop). Payload over 8192 truncated; payload split across writes reads only first chunk -> 'Invalid Request'. Brittle to payload growth/chunking under load. Fix: 4-byte big-endian length prefix, validate 0<len<=Max (reject oversize), loop ReadExactlyAsync until complete; or PipeTransmissionMode.Message + IsMessageComplete.

title: RemExHostControl handoff pipe has no explicit ACL — cross-session takeover fails
description: Boundary: Named Pipe IPC. HostControlServer.cs:53-58 new NamedPipeServerStream with default security, no PipeSecurity. Yield/reclaim handoff is agent(LocalSystem,Session0) <-> GUI(interactive user); default DACL excludes cross-session interactive user; HostControlClient.RequestTakeoverAsync connect denied -> swallowed (HostControlClient.cs:57-62) -> GUI binds canonical port w/o agent yielding -> port-bind race. SUSPECTED unless GUI also runs LocalSystem (verify deployment). Fix: NamedPipeServerStreamAcl.Create granting LocalSystem + Interactive SID.

title: Two divergent IPC stacks (RemExLocalIPC raw-byte vs RemexIPC newline) — name/framing collision

LocalIpcServerService serves pipe 'RemExLocalIPC' raw-byte; IpcHostServer serves pipe 'RemexIPC' (RemExLocalIPC.PipeName) newline-delimited + CurrentUserOnly; static RemExLocalIPC.SendCommandAsync targets 'RemexIPC'+newline. title: paired_clients.json written with no permission hardening (any platform)
description: Boundary: pairing. PairedClientRegistry.PersistToDisk (PairedClientRegistry.cs:109-126) File.WriteAllText+Move, no SetUnixFileMode, no Windows ACL. Windows store under ProgramData (world-readable by Users); Linux inherits umask 0644. Since clientId IS the credential (PAIR-1), read=credential theft, write=self-enrollment. Fix: SetUnixFileMode 0600 (Linux) + restrictive FileSecurity LocalSystem+Administrators (Windows) after Move; harden any secret introduced by PAIR-1 identically.

title: Reconnect auth trusts unbound bearer clientId — no proof-of-possession
description: Boundary: pairing. PairedClientRegistry.IsClientPaired = bare ContainsKey(clientId) (PairedClientRegistry.cs:63-67); RegisterClient stores raw client-supplied clientId (52-61). /ws gate (HostBootstrapper.cs:571, PingPongHandler.cs:126) trusts cleartext clientId; the PIN-derived session key proving possession is discarded. clientId is a 122-bit random UUID under SPKI-pinned TLS (not guessable) but is a long-lived bearer credential with no rotation/PoP; anyone who obtains it (sniff during TOFU pairing handshake, stolen device, registry read per PAIR-4) is authenticated. Fix: persist a per-client secret at pairing; require HMAC challenge-response (server nonce -> HMAC-SHA256(secret,nonce), FixedTimeEquals) per reconnect.

title: Remote desktop input dies after Microsoft 'Windows App' (RDP) disconnects — locked/disconnected session, OpenInputDesktop win32 5
description: Repro: connect to PC with Microsoft Windows App (RDP) over Tailscale, use RemEx alongside; RemEx remote input only works while the RDP client is connected. After it disconnects, RemEx fails with 'could not open the active Windows input desktop (Win32 5: access denied)' (WindowsRemoteDesktopDiagnosticReport.OpenInputDesktop). Root cause: input injection requires an UNLOCKED, connected interactive session. On Windows client, disconnecting RDP leaves the console session LOCKED (secure/Winlogon desktop active) -> OpenInputDesktop access-denied; Windows blocks injection into a locked desktop (security boundary). Reconnecting Windows App unlocks it so RemEx works again. Contributing RemEx weakness: WindowsActiveSession targets WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId only (never the RDP session), and InteractiveDesktopHostLauncher.IsInteractiveHostRunning() treats a GUI host in ANY non-zero session as fine, without checking the session's WTS connect-state -> a host can linger in a disconnected/wrong session. Needs on-machine diagnosis (locked vs disconnected) + session-aware relaunch + clearer 'PC is locked' messaging. Requires user at the PC to test.
close_reason: Verified: InteractiveDesktopHostLauncher now checks IsInteractiveHostRunningInSession(ActiveConsoleSessionId) and relaunches into the active console session rather than trusting a stranded/disconnected-session host (commit 6726c89, InteractiveDesktopHostLauncher.cs:75-83).

title: Remote desktop: cursor never renders on a secondary display at a negative virtual origin (sentinel collision)
description: Client overloads negative coords as a 'cursor hidden' sentinel: RemoteDesktopViewModel sets _hostCursorX/Y=-1f when host reports cursorVisible=false, and mapHostToLocal returns null for any hostX<0||hostY<0. A monitor positioned left-of/above the primary has legitimately NEGATIVE virtual-desktop coords (GetCursorPos), so a real visible cursor there maps to null and never draws (not even the fallback arrow). Positive-origin secondaries (right-of primary) render fine. Fix: decouple visibility from coordinates - add hostCursorVisible flag (host already sends cursorVisible via IsCursorInRegion), stop using -1 sentinel, remove the negative-coord reject in mapHostToLocal, gate the cursor overlay AND the WS1 pan-follow effect on the visibility flag. Found via device test + code trace.
close_reason: Device-verified by user: cursor now renders and tracks on all displays (incl. negative-origin secondaries). Fix: decoupled visibility from coordinates (hostCursorVisible flag), removed -1 sentinel + negative-coord reject in mapHostToLocal, gated overlay + pan-follow on the flag. Commit 923bcbc. Cursor also correctly shows only on the streamed display.

title: Display switch can leave a silent black stream if host is slow to restart (no frame watchdog)
description: Android restartStreamWithCurrentTarget (on display/target switch) does StopDesktopStream, fixed delay(200), then actuallyStartStreaming. If StartDesktopStream silently fails to produce frames (host slow to tear down the previous DXGI capture; 200ms is a guess, not an ack) AND no desktopError is emitted, the stream silently never recovers -> user-visible black screen with no error and no auto-recovery. The unplugged-monitor case self-heals (host emits a DesktopError -> attemptReconnect), but the host-slow case does not. Robust fix: a frame-arrival watchdog (arm on stream start, fire attemptReconnect if no frame decoded within ~7s, cancel on first frame) -- also covers the H264 decoder-init silent-death (RemEx-...). Needs device verification + careful interaction with streamStableJob/reconnect. Partial mitigation already applied (removed premature reconnectAttempts=0 in restartStreamWithCurrentTarget). Found via adversarial review.

title: DXGI: COM leak of _duplOutput/_stagingTexture on partial-init failure during recovery
description: In DxgiDesktopCapture.InitializeDuplication, if DuplicateOutput succeeds (sets _duplOutput) but a later step fails (zero-size output throw, or CreateTexture2D non-S_OK), _duplOutput (and possibly _stagingTexture) is left as a live COM reference. The constructor catch calls ReleaseAll() (safe), and TryReinitializeDuplication pre-releases at its top (self-heals next iteration), BUT TryRecover does NOT pre-release before InitializeDuplication -> on a partial-failure-then-TryRecover sequence the / overwrite the live pointers without Release -> COM leak that accumulates across the ~1s recovery-retry loop during prolonged DXGI-unavailable states (e.g. a flaky driver). Fix: InitializeDuplication now pre-releases _stagingTexture/_duplOutput at its start (Release is null-safe), making every caller leak-free regardless of retry path. Per-frame hot paths verified leak-free. Found via adversarial review.

title: Host FFmpeg H264 encoder lifecycle hardening (stderr deadlock, kill-await, volatile, length-check)
description: Adversarial review of FFmpegH264Encoder found four real lifecycle bugs: (1) CRITICAL stderr drain loop gated on !HasExited could let the OS stderr pipe fill -> ffmpeg blocks -> stdin consumption stalls -> capture-loop frame writes deadlock; and a swallowed exception could strand a running ffmpeg. Fixed: drain to EOF (ReadLineAsync==null) wrapped in try/catch. (2) HIGH DisposeProcess Kill(entireProcessTree) not awaited + reader thread never joined -> on a config-change recreate two ffmpeg processes briefly hold two HW (NVENC) encoder sessions; on capped hardware the new session fails to open -> silent fallback to software/MJPEG. Fixed: snapshot+null fields, Kill then WaitForExit(2s), Dispose, readerThread.Join(2s). (3) HIGH _isDisposed non-volatile, read by reader thread -> marked volatile. (4) MEDIUM EncodeFrame didn't validate input length against ExpectedInputByteCount (a wrong-sized frame permanently desyncs the rawvideo pipe); added a guard returning null on mismatch. All host-side; dotnet test verified. Found via adversarial review.

title: Remote desktop: release all mouse buttons on client disconnect (no stuck button on PC)

The client gesture state machine is correct, but a transport drop mid-drag has no host-side safety net. Added a best-effort release in RemoteDesktopHandler.HandleAsync's finally: after _inputQueue.CompleteAdding(), await the input consumer to drain/exit (bounded 2s, so a queued press can't re-apply after release and no thread races the input device — matters for Linux uinput), then _inputSimulation.MouseUp(0/1/2). Cross-platform via IInputSimulationService; strictly improving (releasing an up button is a no-op). Found via adversarial input-path review.

title: H264 resolution/target switch: two decoders coexist -> HW codec contention can kill stream
description: On a streamPixelWidth/Height change the key() rebuilds the AndroidView; Compose may run the new view's onSurfaceTextureAvailable before the old view's onSurfaceTextureDestroyed. The pointer is identity-guarded (onH264DecoderReleased only nulls activeH264Decoder if it still === the released one) so no dangling pointer, BUT during the overlap two H264StreamDecoders are alive holding two MediaCodec instances. On single-AVC-instance hardware the new createDecoderByType/configure throws 'no more codec instances', self-releases, and the stream silently dies until a reconnect. Fix: release the previous active decoder BEFORE constructing the new one in onSurfaceTextureAvailable (own exactly one decoder via atomic swap+release). HIGH but device-dependent (single-instance HW) and reworks the carefully-ordered surface lifecycle -> needs on-device verification; deferred from the @Volatile/Surface-leak fixes. Found via adversarial review.
close_reason: Verified: single-decoder ownership via atomic swap+guarded release — old decoder released in onSurfaceTextureDestroyed before new created; onH264DecoderReleased identity-guarded (RemoteDesktopScreen.kt:1843-1867).

title: Remote desktop cursor flows drop updates (replay=1, no DROP_OLDEST) -> intermittent disappearance
description: RemexClientManager._desktopCursorState/_desktopCursorShape were MutableSharedFlow(replay=1) with the default extraBufferCapacity=0 + SUSPEND overflow. tryEmit (the host pushes cursor state at ~120 Hz) silently returns false and DROPS when the single collector is mid-handleCursorState. Dropping a position update is harmless, but a dropped visible=false->true transition leaves the overlay stuck hidden, and a dropped shape-serial change desyncs activeCursorShapeSerial so a fresh desktop_cursor_shape is cached but never promoted -> the user-reported 'cursor intermittently disappears'/stale cursor. Fixed by adding extraBufferCapacity + onBufferOverflow=DROP_OLDEST (1 for state, 4 for shape), matching the _frames flow. Found via adversarial review. Code-reasoned; needs on-device verification.

title: Remote desktop MJPEG: fix use-after-overwrite/recycle of the displayed bitmap (Android)
description: RemoteDesktopViewModel.decodeFrame used a single reusableBitmap as the inBitmap target AND published that same Bitmap object to _currentFrame, which Compose draws on the render thread. So the next background decode wrote new pixels into the very bitmap being drawn (in-place overwrite -> tearing + concurrent read/write UB on a non-thread-safe android.graphics.Bitmap). The resolution-change fallback also recycled the previously-published bitmap before swapping the reference, opening a use-after-recycle crash window (the isRecycled guards in RemoteDesktopScreen are check-then-use races). Fix: two-buffer ping-pong (decodeBufferA/B + publishedBitmap) so the on-screen buffer is never the reuse target and no buffer is eagerly recycled; size changes allocate fresh into the off-screen slot. Found via adversarial review. Code-reasoned; needs on-device verification (MJPEG fallback path).

title: Remote desktop host: adaptive encode pacing under send backpressure
description: The capture/encode thread in RemoteDesktopHandler.StreamFramesAsync ran at _targetFps regardless of whether the send loop could drain frames, so on a slow/congested link the host burned CPU encoding (esp. H264/JPEG) frames the sender immediately overwrote/dropped. Added an adaptive encode-pacing controller: smooths the existing 'overwrote an unsent frame' backpressure signal (backpressureEma) and throttles adaptiveFps down (x0.92) when the sender is consistently behind, ramps back up (+2) when caught up, bounded [min(10,target), target] so a low client target is never forced higher. Pure host-side pacing -- no encoder reconfiguration, no wire/protocolVersion change. Surfaced in the 5s metrics log. Code-reasoned; verify CPU/smoothness on-device.

title: Remote desktop: stability-gate the stream reconnect budget (Android)
description: RemoteDesktopViewModel.actuallyStartStreaming reset reconnectAttempts=0 on every (re)start, but StartDesktopStream always succeeds locally even if the stream immediately errors again. So when the main connection is healthy but the desktop stream keeps failing, every retry reset the counter, defeating the escalating backoff (1-2-4-8-16s) and the give-up-after-5 limit -> a ~1s retry storm against the host. Fix: arm streamStableJob on start and reset the counter only after the stream runs uninterrupted for 8s; cancel it on error/stop so the backoff and give-up engage for a persistently-failing stream. Also added +25% jitter to the backoff. Protocol-safe, client-side only.

title: Remote desktop capture: invalidate cached frame on resolution change

Added InvalidateCachedFramesIfResized(): drops caches only when geometry actually changed; transient same-size UAC/lock loss still resumes from last good frame. Part of the Capture-efficiency review; AccumulatedFrames/mouse-only/idle-keepalive already correct; dirty-region partial encode deferred.

title: Remote desktop: vsync-paced H.264 presentation on Android
description: H264StreamDecoder rendered every decoded frame immediately (releaseOutputBuffer render=true) with no display-refresh alignment, so frames arriving with jitter or above the panel refresh caused judder and wasted composites. Added VsyncPresentationScheduler: anchors phase from a Choreographer FrameCallback, takes the interval from the panel refresh rate, schedules each freshest frame onto the next vsync via releaseOutputBuffer(index, renderTimestampNs), and drops frames the panel cannot show (bounding held buffers so decode never stalls). Degrades to immediate render when no vsync anchor / no Context. Code-reasoned only; needs on-device smoothness verification before merge to 2.0.

title: RD cursor: host-composited native cursor intermittently not displayed (~5%)
description: With drawCursor=true the host composites the native cursor into the frame, but it occasionally fails to appear. Suspected DXGI pointer-shape capture intermittency (cursor only reported on change) in the capture/compositing path.
notes: Verification (this session): the DXGI cursor-shape CACHING fix IS present in code — UpdateCursorShape returns null on no-change, GetCurrentCursorShape returns the cached _currentCursorShape, and SyncCursorShapeAsync falls back to the cached shape (RemoteDesktopHandler.cs ~1399-1496). User still observes the ~5% intermittent miss, so either the deployed host predates this fix (redeploy + recheck first) or a deeper DXGI pointer-shape capture race remains. Keep open pending host redeploy + on-device recheck; if it persists, investigate the AcquireNextFrame pointer-shape-only path.
close_reason: Root cause found + fixed: the modern client uses cursor-SHAPE streaming (not host compositing). DXGI TryCaptureCurrentCursorShape returned the cached _lastPointerShape without refreshing; that cache is only updated by the main frame loop, which doesn't run on a static screen — so a cursor-shape change over an unchanging screen (arrow->hand over a link) was missed (~5%). The 10Hz cursor sync now forces a DXGI pointer-shape refresh (reusing the existing null-triggered refresh path, guarded by _lock.Wait(0) so it never races the main loop's AcquireNextFrame). Host builds; tests green (244/244). Requires host redeploy + on-device recheck to confirm the residual ~5% is gone.

title: Agent fails to reliably reclaim the canonical port after the GUI host exits
description: Discovered verifying RemEx-fux. The single-port handoff: GUI host takes over 5005 (agent yields its web host via HostControlServer onYield), and when the GUI host disconnects the agent should reclaim (onReclaim -> AgentCoordinator.StartWebHostAsync -> HostBootstrapper.CreateApplication). Observed FLAKY: in one trial the agent reclaimed 5005 within ~6s; in another the agent process stayed alive but never resumed serving 5005 (still down after ~22s; had to restart the service to recover). Likely cause: CreateApplication's port logic falls back to 5006/5007 when 5005 is briefly busy (GUI socket still in cleanup/TIME_WAIT at the instant reclaim fires), so the agent silently rebinds a NON-canonical port -> Android client can no longer reach the host. (Alternatively onReclaim/StartWebHostAsync intermittently fails.) IMPACT: after logout or a GUI-host crash the PC becomes unreachable from the phone until the service restarts. FIX DIRECTION: in CommandAgent reclaim, bind ONLY the canonical port — wait/retry until it is free, never drift to a fallback (the StalePortReclaimer comment already warns fallback desyncs clients); ensure onReclaim always runs and logs the bound port; add a takeover->kill->reclaim integration test. Part of the epic's 'GUI-host port-takeover reliability'.
close_reason: Implemented wait loop in AgentCoordinator.StartWebHostAsync that polls IsPortFree (extracted from HostBootstrapper) up to 30s before calling CreateApplication, preventing TIME_WAIT drift to fallback ports. Fixed exception cleanup path so _app is nulled on StartAsync failure. Added 3 tests covering wait behavior, full takeover->reclaim cycle, and idempotency guard.

title: LaunchApp from Session 0 silently no-ops (cmd /c start wrapper doesn't surface cross-session)
description: Discovered while verifying RemEx-8bn. AppLauncherService.LaunchInInteractiveSession launches 'cmd.exe /c start "" /D <dir> <target>' via CreateProcessAsUser into the active console session. CreateProcessAsUser returns success and the service logs 'Launched process in interactive session 1', and the IPC/command response is success=true — but NO target process actually surfaces (verified live: triggered LaunchApp for notepad.exe and winver.exe from the Session-0 service; only cmd.exe was created and exited, the target never launched). The cmd/start (ShellExecute) indirection does not work from the Session-0 service context. This is PRE-EXISTING (the startup warning already says 'app launching will NOT work in this session') and is independent of the 8bn lock/monitor-off bridge, which launches our own exe directly (no cmd wrapper) and DOES work. Fix: in Session 0, launch the target exe directly via CreateProcessAsUser (WindowsActiveSession.TryLaunch with applicationName=target) instead of through cmd/start; for non-exe targets/shortcuts, resolve the association first or run a small in-session launcher. Note: command response should also reflect real success rather than returning success when only cmd was created.

notes: EDGE-CASE FIX IMPLEMENTED (compiles: Host build OK, compileDebugKotlin OK, host tests 207/207). Added DesktopMeta.CursorVisible (bool, default true for legacy compat). Investigate: high-refresh capture path, whether NVENC/hardware encode changes the ceiling, and whether a 120Hz host monitor actually yields 120fps. Needs on-PC + capable-phone profiling.

title: Host send loop does not re-check StreamSerial -> stale old-target frame can ship after switch (dormant)
description: RemoteDesktopHandler send loop pulls currentFrame from the buffer and sends it with its stamped StreamSerial without re-checking against the current sessionState.StreamSerial. The capture loop fences correctly (continue on serial mismatch) and HandleTargetSwitchAsync clears the buffer before ResetStream, but there is a window where the capture thread Interlocked.Exchanges an old-serial frame into the buffer just after the clear -> the send loop ships an old-target frame. The client CAN fence on the envelope serial, but the shipping client doesn't use envelopes, so this is latent (dormant with target-switch disabled). Fix: in the send loop, drop currentFrame if currentFrame.StreamSerial != sessionState.StreamSerial (host authoritative). Found via adversarial review.
close_reason: Fixed: send loop now drops any buffered frame whose StreamSerial != session's current serial (RemoteDesktopHandler.cs). Host builds; full test suite green (Core 89 / Client 70 / Host 244).

title: Host target-switch: ResetStream torn serial/sequence (dormant; correctness landmine)
description: DesktopSessionState.ResetStream writes _streamSerial and _frameSequence under lock(_sync), but _streamSerial is read via Interlocked.Read / unlocked capture-loop reads and _frameSequence is incremented via Interlocked.Increment OUTSIDE the lock -> the reset races the capture-loop increment, so a post-switch reset can be clobbered or a sequence appear stale. DORMANT in production (client advertises supportsTargetSwitch=false / supportsFrameEnvelope=false, so ResetStream is never invoked mid-stream), but detonates the moment target-switch is enabled (which code comments suggest is intended). Fix: Interlocked.Exchange for both fields in ResetStream + Interlocked reads in the capture loop, or route all serial/sequence mutation through _sync. Found via adversarial review.
close_reason: Verified: ResetStream mutates serial/sequence under lock(_sync) and all reads use Interlocked.Read/Increment (RemoteDesktopHandler.cs:1426-1495). Torn read/write closed.

title: Input/video: H264 path assumes 1:1 stretch (no letterbox) -> tap drift on mismatched aspect
description: contentRect() returns a zero-letterbox full box for the H264 path (assumes the fillMaxSize TextureView stretches to fill), while the MJPEG path correctly letterboxes. If the host encoded aspect (streamPixelWidth:Height) differs from the on-screen box aspect, the H264 video is stretched and mapLocalToHost (which assumes 1:1 fill) is proportionally off along the mismatched axis -> taps drift on ultrawide/portrait host monitors. Usually small because the box is forced landscape. Fix: apply the same aspect-fit letterbox math to the H264 branch of contentRect() and render the TextureView with a ContentScale.Fit equivalent so input mapping and video agree. Needs on-device verification (changes video layout). Found via adversarial review.
close_reason: Verified: resolved by the 3wr unified-letterbox fix — contentRect() now letterboxes H264 identically to MJPEG and mapLocalToHost uses it for both codecs, so input mapping and video agree (RemoteDesktopScreen.kt:487-532).

title: Input: mapLocalToHost uses Offset.Zero as both error sentinel AND valid host origin (0,0)
description: RemoteDesktopScreen.mapLocalToHost returns Offset.Zero for THREE error conditions (imageSize not laid out, non-finite input, degenerate content rect) but (0,0) is also the legitimate top-left host pixel (primary monitor, hostLeft/Top=0). The stylus contact path (~:776-789) treats any Offset.Zero as 'outside surface -> drop sample' unless the raw view coord was exactly (0,0) -> a stylus tap landing on host (0,0) (top-left hot corner / Start button / maximized window system menu) is silently dropped. Conversely the finger/mouse absolute callers send (0,0) on a genuine not-ready error -> a rare phantom corner click. Recommended fix: change mapLocalToHost to return Offset? (null on the 3 error cases) and update the 7 callers to skip the action on null. Low PRACTICAL impact (1px corner; not-ready only before first frame) but touches 7 sites in critical input code -> deferred from overnight (device-untestable; a mistake could drop all input). Found via adversarial review.
close_reason: Fixed: mapLocalToHost now returns Offset? (null only on the 3 not-ready/degenerate error cases) instead of overloading Offset.Zero as both error sentinel and the valid (0,0) host origin. All 7 callers updated: stylus contact lambda uses a plain null check (no longer the broken vx/vy!=0 hack, so a real (0,0) tap is no longer dropped); stylus hover uses ?: continue; the 5 absolute-mode sends (drag-down x2, abs move, tap-click, long-press right-click) wrap their onSend in hostXxx?.let so a not-ready mapping skips the action instead of firing a phantom (0,0) corner click. Verified: :app:compileDebugKotlin BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Device verification of the corner-tap still recommended.

title: H264 decoder init failure leaves a silently-dead stream (no user feedback/reconnect)
description: If H264StreamDecoder.initializeDecoder's configure/createDecoderByType throws, it is caught and release()d with only a Log.e; the decoder is still published to activeH264Decoder but decodeFrame no-ops forever (decoder null / isConfigured false). Result: a silently dead stream with no user-visible error and no reconnect trigger. Fix: on init failure, signal the ViewModel (surface error -> trigger attemptReconnect or a user-visible 'stream failed' state) instead of only logging. LOW severity (no crash). Found via adversarial review.
close_reason: Fixed: H264StreamDecoder signals onInitFailure -> ViewModel.onH264DecoderInitFailed() stops streaming + reconnects. Android Kotlin compiles clean. On-device verification recommended.

title: H264<->MJPEG codec switch: untyped frame flow can misroute frames mid-switch
description: _frames is a single untyped MutableSharedFlow<ByteArray> with no codec tag/serial; routing is decided at consume time by _activeCodecState.value, updated on a separate coroutine from desktopMeta. On a mid-flight codec switch, frames of the new codec can arrive before the meta flips the flag -> a JPEG fed to the H264 decoder (garbage NAL, caught+dropped) or an H264 NAL fed to BitmapFactory (null, dropped). No crash, but a silent black-frame window with no fence. Proper fix: host tags each frame with codec/stream-serial and client drops mismatches = a coordinated wire-format change (OUT OF SCOPE; protocol frozen without sign-off). Filed for future planning. Found via adversarial review.
close_reason: Fixed: client opts into per-frame RDXF envelope (supportsFrameEnvelope=true) and routes each frame by its own codec tag; legacy untagged frames fall back gracefully. Host+Core build, Android Kotlin compiles, tests green. On-device codec-switch verification recommended.

title: Remote desktop cursorShapeCache grows unbounded (per-session bitmap leak)
description: RemoteDesktopViewModel.cursorShapeCache (ConcurrentHashMap<Long,CursorShapeEntry> keyed by shape serial) stores a new Bitmap/ImageBitmap per distinct cursor shape and never evicts or recycles -> slow per-session memory growth as the user encounters distinct cursors (I-beam, resize arrows, hand, busy-spinner frames, app cursors). Safe re: recycle-while-drawing (nothing recycled), but a real leak. Fix: bound the cache (access-ordered LinkedHashMap, evict >~64) or dedupe by content hash. Found via adversarial review (secondary to the cursor-flow drop bug).

title: Add unit tests for CaptureScaling.ScaledEven (H.264 dimension contract)

It had no tests. Added Remex.Host.Tests/CaptureScalingTests.cs pinning the contract: exact values for exactly-representable scales (1.0/0.5/0.25/0.75), the >=2 minimum clamp, always-even invariant (incl. non-exact scales like 0.6), and determinism. title: Host-generated remote-desktop error strings are English-only on the client

So non-English users see English for these. Proper fix: host sends a stable error CODE (+ optional params) and the client maps it to a localized string. This requires extending the desktop-error message shape -> a coordinated wire-format change, OUT OF SCOPE for the overnight run (must not touch RemexMessage envelope/protocolVersion without sign-off). Filed for future planning. Identified during the localization-completeness work.

title: TypeText breaks non-BMP characters (emoji) — surrogate pairs sent as separate down+up
description: WindowsInputSimulationService.TypeText iterates 'foreach (char c in text)' and sends each UTF-16 code unit as a separate KEYEVENTF_UNICODE down+up via SendOrThrow. For a Unicode char OUTSIDE the BMP (emoji, some CJK-ext), a char is a surrogate code unit, so the sequence becomes high-down, high-up, low-down, low-up. Windows requires the two surrogate code units be sent as CONSECUTIVE keydowns to compose the code point; the intervening key-up breaks it -> emoji/non-BMP typed via the remote keyboard is garbled/dropped. BMP text (virtually all usage) is unaffected. Fix: detect High/Low surrogate pairs (char.IsHighSurrogate/IsLowSurrogate) and send both code units' keydowns consecutively (ideally both INPUTs in one SendInput call) before the keyups. LOW priority (edge case) and touches the text-input hot path -> needs device verification; deferred from overnight to avoid regressing normal typing. Found via direct code review. NOTE: the Avalonia-Key enum mapping in MapKeyCodeToVirtualKey is dead code (all enum values <=255 hit the raw-VK branch first); current Android client sends raw VK, so production key input is correct.
close_reason: Fixed: WindowsInputSimulationService.TypeText no longer sends UTF-16 surrogate pairs with an intervening key-up. Extracted platform-neutral, unit-tested helper UnicodeTextInput.BuildKeyEventGroups: BMP chars -> [down,up]; surrogate pairs (emoji/non-BMP) -> [high-down, low-down, high-up, low-up] sent atomically in one SendInput batch so the two key-downs stay consecutive (required for Windows to compose the code point). Lone/unpaired surrogates typed best-effort as a single code unit. Added UnicodeTextInputTests (8 tests, all pass). Verified: dotnet test --filter UnicodeTextInputTests -> 8 passed. Normal BMP typing unchanged. Device verification of emoji end-to-end still recommended.

title: Harden AdaptiveFrameRateController.CurrentFps cross-thread read (Volatile)
description: Code-review follow-up (cosmetic): CurrentFps (a double read by the send loop for metrics while the capture loop writes it) used a plain field access, which the CLR doesn't guarantee atomic for double -> theoretical torn read on one log line. Publish _currentFps via Volatile.Write in NextFps/Reset and read via Volatile.Read in the getter. _backpressureEma stays plain (capture-thread only). Behavior unchanged; 392 tests pass.
